709.t: String band dances at Deer Range and when it started
709.s: Brass and string bands both played dances, waltzes and jazz, with Jim Robinson in the string band. Kelly says there was no string band when he was a boy and it began after he took up music. Chris Kelly is named among its players.
709.ch: Early life and the plantation brass band
709.q: Sure used to play the dances out there. Sometimes the brass band would play the dances and sometimes the string band played the dances. Jim Robinson and Jim Lindler and all them, we was playing in the old Chester band. Yeah, string band.

259.t: Bands in Baton Rouge and the Hill City band
259.s: Asked about Baton Rouge bands he names George Williams, Spider, Stuart, and the Hill City band with Charlie Vidal, his brother John and Walter Burke.
259.ch: Baton Rouge, Hill City and family music
259.q: Say, who were some of the bands in Baton Rouge? Some of them, well, I didn't know now they got George Williams. You know him George Williams? And uh. Spider used to have a band there, didn't he? Who? Spider. Spider. Oh, Spider, he don't play no more. He was a good corner player, Spider. He don't…

185.t: Uncle's symphony orchestra at St. Catherine's Hall
185.s: Tio recalls playing hooky from his uncle's symphony orchestra rehearsals, and lists the members such as the Gaspard brothers, Professor MacDonald, Nickerson and Camille Nickerson, and other pianists.
185.q: Well, yeah. I remember that because they tried to force me to get in it. Oh, really? And I was, I played hooky from that.

83.t: Mother's family band and the music he grew up hearing
83.s: His aunt and her husband Joseph DiGuardi played piano and clarinet; he heard mazurkas, polkas and marches at family occasions.
83.q: Oh, yes. In fact, my mother's family had quite a lot of people who played music in it. Mm-hmm. And it had what amounted to a family band, you know. Her sister played, her sister played the, Chick Concetta played the piano. Concetta's husband played the clarinet.

456.t: Chamber music concerts at Xavier University
456.s: Violist Cliff Richter persuaded Xavier to host Sunday chamber concerts with about 14 symphony players, which drew packed houses and even Hilsberg; Mazzari likens chamber music to a jazz band.
456.ch: Orchestra people and Xavier chamber concerts
456.q: Oh, uh, yes, Xavier University. Well, I tell you. Uh... Oh, just about the last year before I left New Orleans, Cliff Richter played viola in the symphony and I was playing bass, of course. And, uh, Cliff was teaching at Xavier and he was a very ardent lover of Bach and chamber music and so on and…

574.t: Other country bands and where they played
574.s: Claiborne Williams' band, a Napoleonville band, and Robinson's band playing Thibodaux and towns down the bayou.
574.q: Yeah. I believe you heard them. Yeah. Yeah. They had a band band. They had a little band in Napoleonville. I knew a couple of the fellas. Trombone played by the name of Lewis Hines. Cornet player by the name of, God, it's been so long though. Really that thing kind of slipped me up.

128.t: Brass bands of Day Range, Magnolia and Oakville
128.s: Each community had a fine brass band taught by Humphrey's grandfather; locations of Oakville and St. Sophie are clarified.
128.q: Oh yeah, they had, at my home they had one of the best brass bands in the world. I mean, that country, you understand? They had one band at my home because Pace Unford grandfather took and taught that band. You see? That Day Range band. Magnolia band too. He was one taught son Henry and father.…

808.t: Western swing and country bands in Portland
808.s: She moved from jazz to Western swing with Ranch Dressing, then the country band Beckaroo, and now the duo Cactus Set Up.
808.q: Well I do a little — from the jazz world I went into Western swing, because it’s a logical step to go to Western swing which is a music originated by Bob Wills, a Texas fiddler in what the ‘30s I guess. And he combined Big Band and country music and it really worked. He used a fiddle section and…

1.t: George Jones and Cornelius, the comic duo who played for white ballrooms
1.s: A fat guitarist and a bass player made of twine played Irish songs and Cajun fare for white dances.
1.ch: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
1.q: Drunk Bob. Bob? No, not Bob. A little fat cat with the bass. It's a three-string bass that's made out of twine. And his buddy. You'd see them together. That cat played a whole lot of music, but it would be jive, you know. And he played for ofays. He'd go in White ballrooms, no nigger ballrooms.…

9.t: George Tines and Boston dance bands
9.s: The most popular Black Boston band was George Tines's eight-to-ten piece dance group, in which he mixed up leader and drummer as a boy.
9.ch: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
9.q: : Well, they had Boston bands, you know. They had bands up there. But I can't remember the name. There was a band that did the most work, that was the most popular amongst the Colored people, was George Tines(?). He was a popular band. But there were a lot of bands...

382.t: Dance bands of the 1920s and Homestead's local bands
382.s: They discuss dance bands of the era and the Homestead band her uncle led, and a Whiteman-style concert.
382.q: Well, he had a full brass section -- it was a regular dance band. I imagine besides the things that he might have arranged, he probably played a lot of --
